method.source: frozen M1 difference rasters + common-valid masks
method.threshold_rule: recorded primary threshold of each index (|Δ| ≥ t)
method.geometry: rasterio.features.shapes on the native UTM grid, projected to WGS84 (pyproj); no hand-drawn geometry
method.area_convention: pixel count × pixel area on the projected analysis grid

interpretation.title: ▼ Candidate NDWI decrease · Region 01
interpretation.observed_measurement: Mean ΔNDWI -0.600 index units (median -0.537 index units) at the recorded threshold |Δ| ≥ 0.15; 18,709 px = 187.09 ha = 5.37 % of the 348,129-px shared-valid footprint.
interpretation.meaning: A NDWI decrease here marks where the later composite reads lower in NDWI. In Chilika this most often tracks water-surface extent and exposed lakebed between the two seasons; episodic exposed lakebed is a normal seasonal state, not permanent wetland loss.
explanations: Seasonal water-level change exposing or re-submerging lakebed.
Turbidity and aquatic-vegetation differences between the windows.
Longer-term wetland change — possible, but it cannot be separated from the seasonal signal with one matched pair.
interpretation.evidence_strength: Shared-valid coverage for this comparison is 100.00 % of the AOI (348,129 px). The region is a connected 18,709-px component at a stated threshold — adjacent pixels are not independent observations, so no significance is claimed. Candidate spectral signal with stated thresholds, not independently verified change.
cannot_conclude: That exposed lakebed became permanent wetland loss.
Whether the signal persists outside the compared seasons.

limitations: Water level and seasonality dominate; no hydrological cause claims.
The following indices use 20 m SWIR bands resampled to the 10 m analysis grid and contain no genuine 10 m SWIR detail: mndwi.
Composites are robust within-period summaries of a few observations, not a dense time series; inter-annual change is represented by two period composites only.
Index differences are candidate spectral signals. They are not verified deforestation, wetland loss, construction, glacier damage or any other causal land-cover label.
Cloud, shadow and saturated-pixel exclusion relies on the provider SCL product; terrain shadow is not independently re-derived.
Surface reflectance is the provider L2A product; no independent atmospheric correction is performed.
Areas are planimetric on the documented projected grid; UTM scale distortion at this AOI is small but nonzero.
